figures.caption: TABLE I: Comparison of biosignal datasets and evaluation protocols for assistive intent decoding, highlighting modality coverage, ADL relevance, and whether evaluation is limited to offline open-loop benchmarks or includes system-level closedloop/robot-in-the-loop validation (ours: HIL replay through the full robot stack).

Fig. 2: Overview of the intent-to-commit pipeline: (A) windowed EEG/EMG/ET with masks (acquired through iMotion software); (B) tri-modal resampling and alignment; (C) REST/ACTION segmentation with onsets; (D) sliding windows and LOSO; (E) deterministic preprocessing; (F) commit-as-decision evaluation under sensor dropout S0–S6 with HAC calibration. BP, HP, and LP = Band-pass, High-pass, and Low-pass filters, CAR = common average referencing, Interp. = Interpretation, vel. = velocity.

Fig. 3: NeuroCommitSSM architecture. Masked EEG/EMG/ET windows are tokenized and encoded by modality-specific temporal encoders, then fused via reliability-aware token-level integration. Action/task heads output class probabilities, and a commit head predicts a continuous readiness score ct ∈ [0,1] used for dwell/hysteresis event filtering.
TABLE III: Task classification (LOSO) across sensor dropout scenarios (S0–S6). Reported values are mean±std over folds.
TABLE II: Action detection on LOSO across sensor dropout scenarios (S0–S6). Reported values are mean±std over folds.
TABLE V: Commit decision quality across S4–S6 for FP/1k REST, Flaps/min, and Commit Coverage (%).
TABLE VIII: HIL supervisor ablations on a Kinova Gen3 arm using commit-readiness c(t) and CV-based feasibility fcv(t).
